Du hast schon einmal etwas aufgebaut. Gerade gründest du nicht — aber du willst auch nicht zurück in eine Rolle, in der jemand anderes über Preis, Team und Ergebnis entscheidet. Dann ist das hier deine Rolle: Du übernimmst eines unserer validierten Ventures und führst es als eigenes Unternehmen. Mit Umsatz- und Ergebnisverantwortung, ab Tag 1.

Über hiiive

Wir sind eine AI-First Company mitten in Berlin. Engineering the Future of Intelligence — ROI on Controlled AI.

Wir bauen AI nicht als Demo, sondern als kontrollierte, messbare Wertschöpfung: direkt mit Unternehmen wie Vaillant, Haas Fertigbau oder Telefónica — und über unsere eigenen Software- und Service-Lösungen. Um uns herum arbeitet ein Ökosystem aus Partnern, Spezialisten und Portfolio-Unternehmen.

Wir entwickeln, validieren und skalieren neue Geschäftsmodelle selbst — von der Idee bis in den Markt, mit eigener Technologie, eigenen Daten und echten Kunden. Was an dem Punkt fehlt, an dem ein Venture trägt, ist der Mensch, der es führt. Genau dafür suchen wir dich.

Aufgaben

Deine Mission

Du übernimmst ein bereits validiertes Venture und machst daraus ein Unternehmen, das eigenständig läuft: eigene Kunden, eigene P&L, eigenes Team.

Du bist kein Berater und kein Ideengeber — du bist die kommerzielle Führung. Was verkauft wird, zu welchem Preis, mit welcher Marge und von wem: entscheidest du.

P&L Ownership

  • Volle Verantwortung für Umsatz, Kosten und Ergebnis deiner Einheit
  • Pricing, Angebotslogik und Marge — inklusive der unbequemen Entscheidungen
  • Steuerung auf Zahlen statt auf Gefühl, in monatlicher Taktung
  • Reporting an die Geschäftsführung: Fortschritt, Engpässe, Learnings

Umsatz & Kunden

  • Du verantwortest den Umsatz deiner Einheit — Sales inklusive
  • Die entscheidenden Gespräche führst du selbst: Enterprise-Deals, Verhandlungen, Verlängerungen
  • Aufbau eines wiederholbaren Go-to-Market-Motions statt Einzelfall-Verkäufen
  • Sobald es trägt: Aufbau des Vertriebsteams unter dir

Betrieb & Team

  • Aufbau und Führung des Kernteams — mit Zugriff auf unser Ökosystem aus Partnern, Spezialisten und Freelancern
  • Verantwortung für Delivery-Qualität: was beim Kunden ankommt, verantwortest du
  • Prozesse, die AI-first gedacht sind — nicht Prozesse, die AI nachträglich benutzen

Zusammenarbeit bei hiiive

  • Zugriff auf gemeinsame Ressourcen: Engineering, AI, Legal, Finance, Marketing
  • Austausch mit den anderen Venture-Ownern im Portfolio
  • Enge Taktung mit der Geschäftsführung

Qualifikation

Was du mitbringst

Wir zählen keine Jahre. Uns interessiert nicht, wie lange du wo warst, sondern was du gebaut, verkauft und verantwortet hast — und wie du heute arbeitest.

  • AI-First Arbeitsmodus. Du löst Probleme zuerst mit AI und erst dann mit Headcount. Das ist bei uns kein Nice-to-have, sondern die Voraussetzung.
  • Du hast schon einmal Umsatz verantwortet — als Gründer, Geschäftsführer, Unit Lead oder in einer Rolle, in der die Zahl an dir hing.
  • Du kannst verkaufen. Nicht „Sales steuern" — selbst am Tisch sitzen, verhandeln, abschließen.
  • Du liest eine P&L und triffst danach Entscheidungen.
  • Sicheres Auftreten gegenüber Enterprise-Kunden: Fachbereich, Einkauf, Vorstand.
  • Hohe Ambiguitätstoleranz — du brauchst keine fertige Struktur, du baust sie.
  • Deutsch und Englisch verhandlungssicher.

Gescheiterte Gründungen sind bei uns ein Plus, kein Makel — wenn du sagen kannst, woran es lag.

Wen wir nicht suchen

Damit wir uns beide Zeit sparen:

  • Niemanden, der vor allem eigene Ideen pitchen will. Wir bauen und validieren unsere Ventures selbst — deine Aufgabe ist es, sie zum Laufen zu bringen.
  • Niemanden für Fundraising. Wir bauen aus dem Cashflow, nicht aus Runden.
  • Keine reine Strategie- oder Analyserolle. Ein Deck ersetzt bei uns keinen Abschluss.

Deine ersten 90 Tage

Tag 1–30

Venture, Zahlen und Kunden übernommen; eigene P&L-Sicht steht; erste Kundengespräche selbst geführt

Tag 31–60

Pricing und Angebot geschärft; Pipeline aufgebaut; erste eigene Abschlüsse

Tag 61–90

Wiederholbarer GTM-Motion definiert; Plan für Team und Delivery; belastbarer 12-Monats-Case

Benefits

Was wir bieten

  • Echte Beteiligung an dem Venture, das du führst. Der Umfang hängt von Rolle, Timing und Beitrag ab — wir reden darüber offen im Prozess, nicht erst im Vertrag.
  • Unternehmerische Verantwortung ab Tag 1 — nicht nach der Probezeit
  • Ein validiertes Venture statt einer leeren Seite: Technologie, erste Kunden und Daten sind da
  • Zugang zu unserem Ökosystem: Enterprise-Kunden, Partner, Engineering- und AI-Kapazität
  • Der Weg vom EIR zum Geschäftsführer deiner Einheit ist bei uns der Normalfall, nicht die Ausnahme
  • Attraktives Fixgehalt plus Erfolgsbeteiligung
  • Ein kleines, ambitioniertes Team mit flachen Hierarchien und kurzen Wegen
  • Individuelle Weiterbildungs- und Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten
  • Kostenloses Gym direkt am Büro, regelmäßige Team-Events
  • Büro in Berlin, hybrides Arbeiten nach der Einarbeitung möglich

📩 Bewirb dich jetzt

Du möchtest Verantwortung übernehmen, Kundenwachstum aktiv vorantreiben und ein Team fachlich führen?

Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung inklusive Lebenslauf und kurzer Vorstellung.

title: Senior Venture Architect (m/w/d) – München
description:
nuuEnergy - Das sind WIR!

Unsere Mission: Wir bringen die Wärmewende in die Zukunft und bauen ein System für lokale Handwerks-Betriebe, das Qualität und Effizienz vereint. Das ist nicht einfach und viele sind hier schon gescheitert – bei Qualität, bei Kultur, bei Prozessen. Aber wenn wir diese Challenge meistern, gestalten wir die Zukunft einer ganzen Branche.

Konkret heißt das: Wir entwickeln das Betriebssystem für unsere Wärmepumpen-Standorte deutschlandweit — von Prozessen, über Kundenakquise und Handwerker-Hiring bis hin zu unserer eigenen Software.
Wir sind ein Startup im Aufbau: Vieles entsteht gerade erst, und genau dafür brauchen wir dich. Wir haben top Investoren im Rücken, ein starkes Gründer- & Führungsteam und die Motivation das Handwerk auf ein neues Level zu bringen.


Deine Aufgaben

Als Senior Venture Architect baust du die Strukturen und Systeme, mit denen nuuEnergy skaliert, und steuerst die Unternehmensentwicklung. Aktuell heißt das vor allem: Du bringst unsere Standortleiter zum Laufen. Das heißt du führst sie nicht nur, sondern baust die Systeme, mit denen sie eigenständig performen. Darüber hinaus bist du der unternehmerische Arm der Gründer: Du übernimmst, wo es noch keinen klaren Owner gibt, triffst Entscheidungen im Auftrag der Geschäftsführung und arbeitest cross-funktional mit allen anderen Leads. Kein Verwalter-Job, sondern ein Gestalter-Job.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Standortmodell zum Laufen bringen: ein wiederholbares Modell bauen, mit dem Hubs eigenständig, wirtschaftlich und menschlich stark laufen.
  • Standortleiter zu echten Unternehmern vor Ort entwickeln: technisch starke Menschen bei Führung und Organisation coachen, Konflikte in Handwerksteams lösen und Standards durchsetzen, ohne die Teams zu entmündigen.
  • Wichtige Sonderprojekte schnell von 0 auf 1 bringen und neue Geschäftsmodelle mit Venture Builder Methoden testen & entwickeln.
  • Team- und Orga-Probleme eigenständig lösen (Ziel: der Großteil läuft ohne die Gründer).
  • Personalentscheidungen mittragen — inkl. Trennungen, wenn nötig.
  • A-Player-Quote im Team messbar machen und aktiv steuern.
  • Cross-funktional mit allen Leads relevante Business-Entscheidungen vorbereiten und im Auftrag der Geschäftsführung treffen.
  • Die Geschäftsführung in Meetings, gegenüber Team Leads und extern vertreten.


Dein Profil

  • Deutsch auf C2-Niveau und wohnhaft in München
  • Echte Startup-Erfahrung: Im Aufbau (z.B. Venture Building, Early Stage, Wachstums-Phase) – kein Corporate-Hintergrund.
  • Führungserfahrung: Menschen geführt, aufgebaut und auch harte Personalentscheidungen getroffen.
  • Builder Mindset: Du bist Generalist/in und baust lieber Systeme, als sie zu verwalten.
  • KPI-fokussiert: Du steuerst mit Zahlen, nicht mit Bauchgefühl.
  • Persönlichkeit: Hungrig, hohe Arbeitsbereitschaft, Lust auf Aufbauen unter Unsicherheit.
  • Mobilität: Reisebereitschaft zu unseren Standorten.
  • Branchenerfahrung: Wärmepumpen, Energie, Handwerk, Bau oder dezentrale Servicemodelle (Logistik, Retail, Franchise etc.).


Was dich bei uns erwartet

  • Eine der einflussreichsten Rollen im Unternehmen, direkt an der Geschäftsführung – mit klarer Wachstumsperspektive für jemanden, der liefert.
  • Fixgehalt plus Bonus plus relevante Unternehmensbeteiligung (VSOP) – du baust mit auf und partizipierst am Erfolg.
  • Maximaler Gestaltungsspielraum in einem schnell wachsenden Markt.

Location

While our company operates exclusively on a remote basis, you must reside and have the legal right to work in one of the following countries: the United Kingdom, Latvia, or Spain.

This is a full-time, remote position. Please note that we do not engage on a B2B or contractor basis.

About the Team

Our Finance team is the backbone of Lokalise's financial operations—ensuring accuracy, compliance, and control as we scale. Reporting to the Financial Controller and working closely with FP&A, you will step into a broad, hands-on role.

You will own month-end close and balance sheet integrity across our global entities while acting as the primary internal liaison for our external accounting, payroll, and EOR providers. Additionally, you will champion our finance automation program, transitioning the team from manual workflows to highly scalable, controlled processes.

 

What You Will Do

  • Own the month-end close across multiple entities, managing journals, accruals, reconciliations, and reporting strictly to the group timetable.
  • Own balance sheet integrity, with a specific focus on payroll and employment costs.
  • Act as the internal client for outsourced accounting, payroll, and EOR platforms. Review output, hold them to SLAs, and review/approve payroll across our US, UK, Spanish, Latvian, and EOR entities to meet statutory deadlines.
  • Prepare and post payroll/employment cost journals into the ERP, ensuring data integrity between our HRIS and payroll providers.
  • Provide detailed analysis and actionable commentary on Operating Expenses and other critical areas of the P&L.
  • Lead the charge on documenting and improving workflows. You will transition manual reviews into risk-based, threshold-driven controls.
  • Support annual audits and statutory reporting alongside our auditors and outsourced providers.

 

What You Must Have

  • 5+ years in a hands-on accounting role within a SaaS or tech company, including payroll accounting processes (journals, accruals, and control account reconciliations), month-end close, and balance sheet reconciliations across multiple entities.
  • Professional accounting qualification (ACCA, CIMA, ACA, or equivalent), or qualified by extensive relevant experience.
  • Experience acting as the internal client for external accounting, payroll, or EOR providers — reviewing their output and holding them accountable for accuracy and compliance. A strong accounting foundation is important, alongside experience working with one or more of these provider models.
  • Solid working knowledge of multi-country payroll and payroll-to-GL processes (journals, accruals, and control account reconciliations).
  • Accounting ERP experience and highly advanced Excel/Google Sheet skills.
  • Comfort leveraging AI and automation tools in your day-to-day work, proactively exploring how AI-driven workflows can reduce manual effort and improve controls.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

 

It's a Plus If You Have

  • Wider EU payroll exposure.
  • Experience with EOR providers (Oyster, Deel, Remote, Papaya).
  • Experience migrating to or implementing a cloud ERP.
  • Experience with Rillet, Ramp, Stripe or Xero.

 

Our Benefits

💰 Competitive salary and employee stock options.

🌍 Fully remote setup with flexible working hours.

🏢 Co-working budget for those days you want a change from your home office.

🌴 Flexible vacation policy to recharge when you need to.

🖥️ Home office setup budget: monitor, desk, ergonomics, whatever helps you do your best work.

📚 Learning & development budget to grow your skills and career.

🏥 Health insurance to keep you covered.

🧘 Wellness allowance to support your mental and physical well-being.

title: Payment Operations Lead
description:
Payment Operations Lead

Global expansion is broken. Without a local company, conversion rates fall, costs rise, and compliance gets messy. Outpost fixes it.

Selling internationally is a maze of tax, payments, and operational friction. Most brands avoid it, or expand slowly and expensively.

Outpost is your modular back office for global commerce.

Pick only what you need - tax, payments, treasury, or operations - and unlock new markets without the overhead. Sometimes we become liable for a merchant's taxes. Sometimes we become the legal reseller in each market and carry the payments, tax and compliance risk. Other times, we give you the tools to do it yourself.

We go live wherever a merchant needs to sell next, for digital and physical goods. That means we own the full stack - payments, tax, compliance, treasury, and merchant experience.

Sell anything, anywhere. Without compromise.

🧠 The Role

We're looking for a Payment Operations hire to own the part of Outpost where the money actually moves.

When we become the legal reseller in a market, we take the payment. Every merchant we onboard gets its own merchant ID and its own merchant category code, never pooled into one shared code, which is exactly why our approval rates beat the alternatives. Keeping that true across every market, every processor and every merchant is the job.

This is a quantitative role in an operational seat. You'll live in the transaction data: why authorisation rates differ by market, issuer, card type and hour of day, what a routing change is actually worth, where a 40 basis point cost difference is hiding, which decline codes are recoverable and which are noise. Then you'll act on it, with processors, with engineering, and with merchants.

You won't be siloed. Payments at Outpost touches pricing, treasury, tax and the product roadmap, and you'll be pulled into all of it. But your edge is the numbers, and we want someone whose first instinct on any problem is to pull the data and model it.

You'll work directly with the founding team and with engineering, who will build what you spec.

🧗 What You'll Get

Yes, the work is intense. But in return you'll get scope and exposure most people wait 10 to 20 years to access.

You'll own economics that decide whether the company is profitable, negotiate with processors and banks as a principal rather than a customer, and get to see the full machinery of cross-border payments from the inside. We won't handhold, but we'll coach you hard.

🧩 What You'll Do

Build the system

  • Run payment operations agentically. Build agentic system that monitor approval rates, triage declines, assemble dispute evidence, chase reconciliation breaks and draft the processor follow-up, so humans only touch the exceptions. You'll design the workflows, set the guardrails, and audit what the agents produce

  • Write the playbooks: new processor onboarding, new market launch, incident response, dispute handling

  • Onboard new processors, banking partners and local acquiring as we launch new markets

Own payments performance

  • Own approval rates by market, processor, issuer, card type and merchant, and know why each one moves

  • Build and run routing logic. Decide what goes where, prove the uplift, and iterate

  • Run decline recovery: retry logic, network tokens, account updater, 3DS strategy and exemption handling

  • Run chargeback operations and fraud strategy. Set thresholds, represent disputes, keep merchants inside scheme limits

  • Own the payment incident path. When authorisations drop in one market at, you're the one who spots it and fixes it

Own the economics

  • Build full visibility into cost per transaction: scheme fees, interchange, processor margin, FX, and where each one leaks

  • Own processor relationships day to day. Performance reviews, pricing negotiations, new partner evaluation

  • Model the trade-off between approval rate and cost by market, and make the call

  • Feed real payment economics into how we price merchants

Own the money movement

  • Settlement, reconciliation and payouts. Every penny accounted for, every break chased down

  • Reserve logic and settlement timing by merchant segment and risk profile

  • Work with treasury on funding, FX exposure and cash timing across our local companies

💥 Example Projects

  • Take a market from a 66% approval rate to 90% or better, and prove exactly which changes did it

  • Build the routing framework that optimises approval rate against cost, market by market

  • Renegotiate processor pricing using our own volume and performance data

  • Build the cost-per-transaction model across every processor and market, and find the basis points nobody is watching

  • Debug delays in settlement and fix them across engineering, operations and the processor

  • Design reserve and settlement logic for a new merchant segment and implement it

  • Cut chargeback rate through better fraud tooling and merchant policy

  • Evaluate and onboard a new processor for local acquiring in Latin America or Asia

  • Build the payments monitoring layer so anomalies find us, not the other way round

🧱 What We're Looking For

Ideal background:

  • A STEM or quantitative degree is strongly preferred - mathematics, physics, engineering, computer science, statistics, econometrics or similar.

  • 3 to 7+ years in payment operations, payment analytics, or a data or analytics role that moved into payments, at a processor, acquirer, or high-volume fintech (Adyen, Stripe, Checkout.com, Nuvei, Worldpay, Revolut, Wise, Dojo, Airwallex or similar)

  • Strong analytical skills — advanced Excel or Sheets, experience with BI tools, and the ability to build models and run analyses independently without waiting for a data team.

  • Bonus: experience at platforms that act as the legal reseller (Global-e, Digital River, Paddle), local acquiring outside Europe and the US, interchange and scheme fee economics, or a background in data science or quantitative consulting before payments

Signals we care about:

  • Ridiculous bias for action. You solve, you don't observe

  • Analytically strong and commercially sharp. You quantify the opportunity before you argue for it

  • Systems thinker who still does the work. You fix the transaction, then remove the reason it broke

  • Strong EQ. Processors, banks and merchants all need managing, often at the same time

  • Exceptionally hard working. You see work as a core part of your purpose

  • Fluent in ambiguity and chaos. Startups are not neat, this will be hard

  • Curious and resourceful. You can figure anything out

  • Clear, quantified achievements on your CV, not vague descriptions

What this role is not:

  • Not a payments strategy role without operational depth. You'll be in the dashboards daily

  • Not a pure analytics role. The analysis is the start, the change is the job

  • Not a narrow specialist seat. Payments here touches pricing, treasury, tax and product

  • Not for someone who needs defined processes and hierarchy to be effective

🚀 Why This Role Is Different

Most companies treat payments as a cost centre someone else manages. Here it is the product and the margin at the same time.

We take legal responsibility for our merchants' payments. That means a point of approval rate is real revenue for them and real evidence for us, and a basis point of cost is real profit. Very few people get to own that surface this early, with this much data and this little bureaucracy in the way.

We expect whoever is in this role to grow rapidly, and we'll back you every step of the way.

🦾 Outpost Team

Our team were leaders at Revolut, Airwallex, Adyen and Wayflyer, and we're backed by top-tier investors who have built or backed some of the world's leading fintechs.

🧾 What We Offer

  • Equity and salary in a well-funded startup

  • Ability to own your work and move fast

  • World-class training from operators who've scaled globally

  • A global mission with real impact

  • Low politics, high output

  • Chance to grow into a senior leadership role

  • A culture of builders, not talkers

🧭 Working Style

We work together in person in London 5 days a week. We believe the hardest problems are solved in the room.

🌎 Reach Out

Learn more

  1. Outpost Culture

  2. Outpost founder

Outpost is where the hard problems are. If you want to help build the engine behind global trade, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Complaints Handler
description:
📍 Based in our Lincoln City Centre office 2 days per week with the remaining 3 days working remotely (or office if you prefer!)

Our mission:

  • Two in five people in the UK rent their homes. Our mission? To provide them with the best renting experience in the world

  • We started Goodlord because we wanted to make renting simple and transparent for everyone involved: the agent, the landlord, and the tenant. We knew Generation Rent would lead to more tenants, with higher digital expectations and we were confident we could provide a solution

  • Like all scale-ups it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster journey, but we’re now stronger than ever, with around 3,000 letting agents using the platform, exciting and varied products and 350+ Goodlordians across the group supporting the mission!

The Opportunity

You’ll be part of our central complaints function, ensuring customers receive timely, fair and regulated complaint resolutions.

You’ll:

  • Manage our complaints inbox and ensure acknowledgements and timelines are met

  • Handle complaints in line with FCA and internal procedures

  • Maintain accurate records, notes and documentation

  • Investigate cases thoroughly using internal systems and cross-team collaboration

  • Write high-quality final response letters addressing all aspects of a complaint

  • Spot patterns and work with teams to improve processes

What we need from you

  • Proven experience in written complaint handling as your main responsibility

  • Strong written communication skills and the ability to write structured, well-reasoned responses

  • A solid understanding of regulated complaint requirements, timelines, and evidential standards

  • Investigative nature, with the ability to assess information to reach a reasoned conclusion for the complainant

It would also be great if you have:

  • Experience in an Insurance environment regulated by the FCA (e.g. home insurance, motor, general insurance, property insurance etc)

  • Working knowledge of the Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS)

  • Understanding of the residential lettings sector, specifically the process of tenant referencing

Why you'll love being a Goodlordian

Aside from the role, the people, our culture and our mission, we have some other things that make Goodlord a pretty awesome place to be. Here’s a few favourites amongst Goodlordians (check out our careers page for more info).

  • Grow with Goodlord: your development is important to us, that’s why we are Great Place to Work - certified. Have a goal in mind? Share it with us so we can use some of our annual development fund to support it. We guarantee you’ll learn loads and develop both personally and professionally!

  • Your well-being matters: bi-weekly coaching with Sanctus to provide Goodlordians with a safe place to talk and support your mental health

  • 25 days holiday (plus UK Bank holidays) plus 1 day per full holiday year up to 32 days: We believe regular breaks are essential for well-being and we encourage (some may say expect!) all Goodlordians to take full advantage of their annual leave entitlement.

  • Supporting your family: we offer Goodlordians of all genders a generous 3 months of fully-paid time off to look after their new arrivals

  • Our team: we’re an energetic, sociable, and talented bunch who are super passionate about what we do and determined to make a difference. We’re all in it together, we learn from each other, we’re genuine and we don’t have time for politics

What’s next?

If you’re ready to help us on our mission to be the gold standard platform for renting, then click apply (2-3 minutes)!

A full job spec is available on request.

Goodlord wants applicants from all backgrounds and walks of life; we are an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive environment.

Creating a space where everyone feels included is central to who we are. Because we're an open book and we learn from each other, we actively champion diverse perspectives and unique life experiences. If there is anything you need to participate fully in the interview process, we'd love to hear about that too - please include it in your application.


** Please note, as we are regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority, all Goodlordians are required to pass a thorough referencing check via Experian before joining the team. We will only ask for references at the point of making an offer.

No agencies please - we have tried and trusted partners we would turn to should we require support.
